lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 6 you met unit rates. A car goes 150 km in 3 hours. How far does it go in 1 hour? 150 ÷ 3 = 50 km.
Speed tells you how far something goes in each unit of time: speed = distance ÷ time. A cyclist rides 36 km in 2 hours, so the speed is 36 ÷ 2 = 18 km/h (kilometres per hour).
The formula triangle helps: cover the one you want. Distance = speed × time, and time = distance ÷ speed. At 18 km/h, 54 km takes 54 ÷ 18 = 3 hours.
Average speed = total distance ÷ total time, stops included. A 90 km trip with 2 hours of driving and a 30-minute stop takes 2.5 hours: 90 ÷ 2.5 = 36 km/h.
To change km/h into m/s, divide by 3.6, because 1 km is 1,000 m and 1 hour is 3,600 seconds: 36 ÷ 3.6 = 10 m/s. To change m/s into km/h, multiply by 3.6.
A distance-time graph shows a journey: time goes along and distance goes up. A steeper line is faster, and a flat line means stopped. Leg A covers 6 km in 30 minutes: 12 km/h.
Speed matters on roads. A driver needs time to react. At about 13 m/s (48 km/h), a car goes about 9 m before the brakes start. It needs about 23 m to stop.
Try it in the world: time a 100-block walk in your world (a block is 1 m) and find your speed in m/s. In LIFE, Safe Streets shows why a fast car needs a long way to stop. Next: expressions.

exercises.prompt: A runner covers 400 m in 80 seconds. What is her average speed in m/s?
exercises.hint: Divide the distance by the time.

exercises.prompt: A train travels at 120 km/h for 2 hours. How far does it go, in km?
exercises.hint: Cover distance on the triangle: what is left?

exercises.prompt: Which formula gives the time a journey takes?
exercises.hint: Cover time on the triangle: what is left, and which is on top?
exercises.explain: Covering time leaves distance over speed: time = distance ÷ speed.

exercises.prompt: Match each calculation to what it finds.
exercises.hint: Picture the triangle: distance on top, speed and time below.
exercises.explain: Distance ÷ time gives the speed; speed × time gives the distance; distance ÷ speed gives the time.

exercises.prompt: On a distance-time graph, a flat line means the object has stopped.
exercises.hint: If the distance does not change while time passes, is it moving?
exercises.explain: True: the distance stays the same, so it is not moving.

exercises.prompt: Write 2 hours 30 minutes in hours, as a decimal.
exercises.hint: What fraction of an hour is 30 minutes?
exercises.explain: 30 minutes is half an hour, so 2 hours 30 minutes is 2.5 hours.

exercises.hint: From km/h to m/s, divide by 3.6.
From m/s to km/h, multiply by 3.6.

exercises.prompt: A bus travels 30 km in 45 minutes. What is its speed in km/h?
exercises.hint: Change 45 minutes into hours first, then divide.

exercises.prompt: The graph shows Zara's walk. What was her speed on leg C, in km/h?
exercises.hint: Read leg C's distance and time, then work out the distance in one hour.
exercises.explain: Leg C: 4 km in 30 minutes, which is 8 km in 60 minutes: 8 km/h.

exercises.prompt: Order these speeds from the slowest to the fastest.
exercises.hint: Change every m/s into km/h first (× 3.6), then compare.
exercises.explain: 10 m/s = 36 km/h and 20 m/s = 72 km/h, so: 30 km/h, 10 m/s, 50 km/h, 20 m/s.

exercises.prompt: Sort the speeds: faster or slower than 50 km/h?
exercises.hint: Change each m/s into km/h by multiplying by 3.6.
exercises.explain: Faster: 15 m/s (54 km/h), 60 km/h and 20 m/s (72 km/h). Slower: 12 m/s (43.2 km/h), 40 km/h and 10 m/s (36 km/h).

exercises.prompt: The graph shows Bram's bike ride. On which leg was he fastest?
exercises.hint: The steepest part of the graph is the fastest.
exercises.explain: Leg C rises 4 km in 10 minutes (24 km/h). Leg A is 12 km/h, leg D 6 km/h, and leg B is a stop.

exercises.prompt: A family drives 150 km in 2 hours, stops for 30 minutes, then drives 60 km in 1 hour. What is the average speed for the whole trip, in km/h?
exercises.hint: Add all the distances and all the times, the stop too, then divide.

exercises.prompt: Thunder is heard 3 seconds after the lightning. Sound travels about 340 m/s. About how far away is the storm, in metres?
A car travels at 13 m/s. The driver takes 0.7 seconds to react. How far does the car go before braking starts, in metres?
exercises.hint: Multiply the speed by the reaction time.
exercises.explain: 13 × 0.7 = 9.1 m: this is the thinking distance.

exercises.prompt: A car at 72 km/h is faster than a cheetah sprinting at 25 m/s.
exercises.hint: Change 72 km/h into m/s by dividing by 3.6, then compare.
exercises.explain: False: 72 ÷ 3.6 = 20 m/s, which is slower than 25 m/s.

exercises.prompt: Light from the Sun takes about 500 seconds to reach the Earth, at about 300,000 km/s. About how far away is the Sun, in km?
exercises.hint: Multiply the speed by the time, and count the zeros carefully.

exercises.prompt: Mo rides 12 km out at 12 km/h and 12 km back at 24 km/h. What is his average speed, in km/h?
exercises.hint: It is not halfway between the speeds: find each time first.
exercises.explain: Out: 1 hour. Back: 0.5 hours. 24 km ÷ 1.5 hours = 16 km/h.
